The application is a server-rendered catalog management website with an optional image-upload endpoint. It runs as a single .NET Framework application and uses configuration-selected implementations for data, identity, and image storage.

Data Storage & External Services

Catalog records are stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6. Azure Blob Storage is an optional image backend; local images are used by the mock implementation. Azure Active Directory, Key Vault, Application Insights, and Redis-backed session state are configuration-dependent integrations. No message broker communication was found in the application source.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or database-backed catalog services and local or Azure image storage from configuration.
  • Entity Framework owns relational persistence; catalog images are stored separately from catalog metadata.
  • The application uses server-rendered Web Forms and an ASMX method rather than a separate REST API or gateway.

DTOs & Contracts

There are no dedicated request/response DTO classes. CatalogItem is the catalog entity used by the service and Web Forms pages; PaginatedItemsViewModel carries listing results. PicUploader.UploadImage returns an anonymous JSON object with name and url properties. The response is serialized with JavaScriptSerializer. No immutable record DTOs, protobuf schemas, GraphQL schemas, or OpenAPI documents were found.

Communication Patterns

Browser requests and Web Forms postbacks are synchronous. CatalogService uses EF6 against SQL Server, and ImageAzureStorage calls Azure Blob Storage when enabled; the alternative mock service serves local seeded data. The application does not implement a gateway, service discovery, asynchronous messaging workflow, retry policy, circuit breaker, or bulkhead. A Service Bus package is declared, but no runtime message-broker use was identified.

OpenID Connect with cookies is configured conditionally through OWIN and Azure Active Directory. The Create, Edit, and Delete pages issue a sign-in challenge when the request is unauthenticated. When Azure Active Directory is disabled, the configured fallback middleware constructs a claims identity locally rather than performing an external sign-in. No role-based authorization checks or application-level HTTPS enforcement were found. Image upload authorization is not checked in PicUploader.UploadImage.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. IIS or the web container starts the application and reads Web.config.
  2. Configuration builders resolve environment, user-secrets, and optional Key Vault values.
  3. OWIN configures OpenID Connect when Azure AD is enabled; otherwise the configured fallback middleware is used.
  4. Global.Application_Start registers routes and bundles, builds the Autofac container, configures the database initializer, initializes images, and installs telemetry.
  5. In database-backed mode, the application requires the configured SQL Server connection when database initialization or a catalog request occurs; Azure Blob Storage is required only when enabled.

Docker Compose defines a SQL Server health check but no explicit depends_on or application wait-for-ready mechanism.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing a product catalog and maintaining catalog items, brands, types, stock levels, and product images. Its workflows are handled within one Web Forms application rather than across independently deployed business services.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog managementProduct offered in the catalog, with price, stock, and image referenceBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog managementBrand associated with catalog itemsCan be referenced by many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalog managementCategory/type associated with catalog itemsCan be referenced by many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog managementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server through EF6; optional Azure Blob Storage for images

The application is a single bounded context. No inter-service events or remote domain APIs were identified.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the default page or a route containing pagination values.
  2. The page requests a catalog page from ICatalogService.
  3. The service loads items and their brand/type relationships from the selected database or mock provider.
  4. The page resolves image URLs and renders the page. When mock mode is active, the service uses its in-memory seeded list.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. An administrator opens the create or edit page; the page triggers an OpenID Connect challenge when the request is not authenticated.
  2. The browser submits the item fields and selected brand/type.
  3. The page checks ModelState, parses numeric fields, and constructs a CatalogItem.
  4. The catalog service assigns or uses the item ID and persists the item.
  5. If a temporary image is present, the image service promotes it to the item's image location and the page redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Upload a catalog image

  1. The browser posts the image and item ID to PicUploader.UploadImage.
  2. The endpoint decodes the upload and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF image formats.
  3. The configured image service stores the file in Azure Blob Storage when enabled, or returns the mock implementation's configured image behavior.
  4. The endpoint returns the image name and URL as JSON for use by the catalog form.

Workflow 4: Delete a catalog item

  1. An administrator opens the delete page, which challenges unauthenticated users when configured.
  2. The page resolves the catalog item by route ID.
  3. On postback confirmation, the catalog service removes the entity and the page redirects.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service aggregation or domain data exchange was found. Catalog metadata is sourced from the local SQL Server database or mock list. Images are stored separately through the optional Azure Blob backend; the application combines the image URL with catalog item data when rendering pages.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin as "Catalog administrator" participant Page as "Create page" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant DB as "SQL Server" participant Image as "Image service" participant Blob as "Azure Blob Storage" Admin->>Page: Submit item fields and temporary image reference Page->>Page: Check page model state and parse fields alt Input accepted Page->>Service: CreateCatalogItem(item) Service->>DB: Save catalog item DB-->>Service: Save completed opt Temporary image was uploaded Page->>Image: Promote temporary image Image->>Blob: Copy image to item location Blob-->>Image: Copy accepted end Page-->>Admin: Redirect to catalog else Input invalid Page-->>Admin: Return form with validation state end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog items require an associated brand and type; EF mappings define these required relationships.
  • Price is constrained to non-negative values with at most two decimal places. Stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock values are range-constrained in the model.
  • The application selects database-backed or mock catalog storage, and local or Azure image storage, from feature settings.
  • A new catalog item ID is allocated through the HiLo sequence in database mode or from the current maximum ID in mock mode.
  • EF SaveChanges persists catalog mutations; no distributed transaction, saga, or message-driven workflow was found.
  • Page code logs request entry and uses OWIN authentication configuration for selected administrative pages; no role-specific business authorization was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy Web Forms, EF 6.3, OWIN, and older Azure SDK packages. Moving to a modern .NET target requires substantial framework and application changes; the .NET 10 upgrade assessment records package incompatibilities and project-format work.

Notable Observations

  • The package inventory includes 147 entries because packages.config lists framework-support dependencies alongside primary libraries.
  • Application Insights, Azure Storage, Key Vault, and Redis packages are present, but their use is configuration-dependent.
  • WindowsAzure.ServiceBus is declared, though no corresponding runtime call was found in source.
  • No test-scoped package entries or separate test project were detected in this workspace.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application persists a small catalog domain in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6. The model contains three relational entities, with optional mock data and image storage used for local or configured deployments.

Database Configuration

Catalog applicationSQL ServerDatabase-backed modeEF6 SQL Server providerCatalogDBContext connection string supplied through configuration builders; managed identity is an optional connection pathNo migration tool detected; CreateDatabaseIfNotExists initializer and SQL sequence scripts are used
Catalog applicationIn-memory mock dataUseMockData enabledNoneCatalogServiceMock seeded from preconfigured dataNot applicable

Customization data can be loaded from CSV files and images from a ZIP archive under Setup. Database seed scripts create the HiLo sequences. No Flyway, Liquibase, EF migration set, or separate schema migration runner was found.

Entity Model

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ Catalog : "labels" CatalogType ||--o{ Catalog : "classifies" CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type } Catalog { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogTypeId FK int CatalogBrandId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder }

CatalogItem is mapped to the Catalog table, with required foreign keys to CatalogBrand and CatalogType. The entity classes are Models/CatalogItem.cs, Models/CatalogBrand.cs, and Models/CatalogType.cs; the mappings are in Models/CatalogDBContext.cs. No explicit transaction annotations were found; EF6 SaveChanges is used for individual mutations.

No repository interfaces separate the EF context from CatalogService; there are no cross-service bulk query methods.

Caching Strategy

No catalog entity cache, query cache, or distributed data cache is configured in the application code. A Redis session-state provider dependency and commented sample configuration are present, but the sample does not actively enable that provider. When mock mode is selected, CatalogServiceMock is a singleton with a shared mutable in-memory catalog list.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The catalog application is a single bounded context backed by one SQL Server database; it has no database-per-service or cross-service data exchange. Catalog brands and types are related to catalog records through foreign keys. Mock mode replaces persistence with an in-memory list. The optional Redis package concerns session state rather than catalog ownership.
